reason: Reinforcing the bone framework directly matches a goal, and the picture shows mineral resisting a push.
expectation: I expect the mineral to make the framework harder and better able to resist compression.

alternatives.reason: Grouping the muscle cells also matches a goal, but I want to build the bone first.

effect: The mineral reinforced the living bone, and joining the bones at the elbow is now a goal.
reaction: It was interesting that bone stays living tissue even with hard mineral in it.
reason: The elbow joint should connect the arm bones, directly advancing the new goal.
expectation: I expect the bones to be joined at the elbow, with the joint allowing movement.

alternatives.reason: Building the muscle tissue also meets a goal, but I want to finish connecting the bones first.

effect: The bones now form a movable skeleton, with ligaments bracing the elbow and cartilage and fluid separating its moving surfaces.
reaction: The picture helped me understand what holds and separates the joint.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it matches the goal of grouping muscle cells in supporting tissue.
expectation: I expect the muscle cells to be grouped together with supporting tissue, though I don't know exactly what the resulting structure will look like.

effect: The muscle cells formed bundles with tendon ends, ready to connect to the skeleton.
reaction: The time strip made the change from cells to bundles clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination and matches the new goal of connecting pulling tissue to the skeleton.
expectation: I expect the tendons to connect the muscle bundles to the arm bones, though I don't know exactly how they will be arranged.

effect: The completed arm shows how muscles on opposite sides pull to bend and straighten the same elbow.
reaction: The two views made the opposite pulls easy to picture.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the muscle bundles to the skeleton was most worthwhile: the two views showed how pulling muscles move the elbow in opposite directions.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grouping the muscle cells was useful, but less engaging as a decision because it was the only combination offered.

surprise.text: I was interested that hard bone still contains living cells and blood vessels.

arbitrary.text: None felt clearly arbitrary; the combinations matched the goals and pictures, even when only one was available.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing the separate parts come together into a working arm made me curious about other body systems.
